title: Events Management Policies and Procedures Manual

nodes.heading: Introduction
nodes.own_text:
This manual compiles policies and procedures for organizing, running, and closing
events. The actual technical content of the event is set aside as the manual’s main
purpose is to focus on the management aspect of events.
Events at GHD|EMPHNET may take several forms that vary in complexity and
arrangement requirements. However, the running of all these events shall include
planning, preparation, conduct, and closeout.
For the purpose of this manual, an Event is defined as Assessment, Field Outreach,
Meeting, Regional Meeting, National/sub-national or Regional Training Workshop or
another Training Event, as well as Conferences/Symposia, where:
Regional/Global Conferences and/or Scientific Symposia: These regional/
global events require extensive planning, preparation, implementation, and
closeout efforts. While general elements of this manual are applicable to each
of such high-level events, they may come with their own guidance/guideline as
needed. (Conference details are covered in separate document).
Regional training workshop: Regional-level training for participants from
multiple countries.
Country training workshop: National and subnational training workshop.
Regional
workshop/
meeting: Non-training
key
event
attended
by
participants from the region e.g. NITAG regional meetings, FETP Directors’
meetings, etc.
Country workshop/ meeting: Non-training workshops or meetings that may
include meetings with national stakeholders.
Field outreach: activities that include field work and reach out such as
awareness campaigns, vaccination campaigns, engagements and meetings
with local communities, field visits to health centers, community centers, FETP
fieldwork, etc.
Assessment/ Field Study: the event pertains to conducting an assessment
and studies and include data collectors’ trainings, data collection field visits,
focus group discussions, meetings, etc.
GHD|EMPHNET’s Executive Director has the authority to approve and sign this
manual according to the endorsed authority matrix. The Organizational Development
has the responsibility of reviewing the manual and ensuring its consistency with
internal policies and procedures and in compliance with best practices and internal
controls. The involved parties (Technical Team including the Operations team, Project
Management Office, Media and Communication, Information Technology Team) in
this manual have the responsibility to review and keep this manual updated based on
the adopted manuals review procedures and authority matrix.
The Organizational Development and Quality Management are responsible of
performing regular reviews and monitoring to identify possible risks and to guarantee
that all measures are taken to prevent breaching of policies and/or procedures.

GHD|EMPHNET has the right to amend the policies mentioned in this manual at any
time. Failure to comply with any of the policies will be considered actionable behavior
by senior management and could result in disciplinary action up to and including
suspension or termination.

nodes.heading: Purpose of the Manual
nodes.own_text:
This manual aims to provides GHD|EMPHNET staff with the policies and procedures
to assure systematic and standardized implementation of events with clear
responsibilities and authorities within a specific timeline. The manual will ultimately
minimize concerns and problems as it is based on GHD|EMPHNET’s experience in
running events over the years.

nodes.heading: Manual Overview
nodes.own_text:
Planning and timely organization are essential for effective event management. In
addition, teamwork with regular, clear, and timely communication are all essential
elements for producing successful events. This document contains information to
make events successful and effective from the planning till the close-out phase. This
manual covers the following sections:
Planning and preparation phase.
Event Implementation phase
Closing the event

nodes.path: Section 01: Planning and Preparation for the Events

nodes.heading: 1.1. Purpose
nodes.own_text:
This section aims to set the policies, procedures, and guidelines for planning and
preparation phase for events conducted by GHD|EMPHNET.

nodes.heading: 1.2. Scope
nodes.own_text:
Planning for an event is essential for assuring successful results. It requires team
effort, multitask management, communication, coordination, and collaboration.
Planning helps in implementing successful actions and in making decisions that can
prevent failure or mistakes. This section presents the major areas that need to be
considered when planning an event. These topics are not inclusive as it is impossible
to plan for any unforeseen occurrence which are bound to occur even with the best
plans. The covered topics are standard issues that need to be considered when
planning an event to take place in regular and steady circumstances. This section
applies to all personnel involved in planning and preparation phase.

nodes.heading: 1.3. Responsibilities
nodes.own_text:
It is the responsibility of the Task Owner to initiate the process for the event,
and to provide the required information to the involved stakeholders to assure
timely and proper preparation for the event.
When the event is conduct outside Jordan, it is the responsibility of the Task
Owner to make the required arrangements with the representative in the
country.
It is the responsibility of the Operations Officer to arrange for all required
logistics to prepare for the event on timely manner and according to the event
requirements and the policies mentioned in this section
It is the responsibility of the relevant employee from Project Management Office
to monitor the implementation of the event according to the Gantt Chart and the
event plan.
It is the responsibility of the Media and Communication Team to make all the
required arrangements according to the Task Owner’s request.
It is the responsibility of the Finance Department to make sure that the event
expenses are in alignment with the event predefined budget.
Other responsibilities are detailed in the below policies and procedures.

nodes.heading: Planning
nodes.own_text:
g
Advanced planning of events is crucial for successful implementation. All
GHD|EMPHNET events are planned ahead of time in order to secure ample time for
preparation. When organizing events, it is important to keep in mind the timeframe and
entailed costs. Once the exact dates of the event are formally set in coordination
between Technical and Project Management teams, the Task Owner shall initiate
Event Request Process on the system at least one month before the event start date.
(Note: Sometimes the exact dates are not agreed upon till closer to the event. In this
case, the event can be initiated and start preparations while waiting for the
determination of the dates.)
Before starting the process on the system, the Task Owner shall ensure proper
planning, acquire needed approvals, and collection of the required data to initiate the
process. At this stage, and to make sure of appropriate planning, our representatives
in the countries could be consulted whenever the need arises. The Task Owner shall
be are aware that the below data provide the road map for the preparation and conduct
of the event and they will function as the guidelines and instructions for the different
departments. It is important to be aware that not all these field are considered required
for all events, this depends on the event nature, requirement and complexity.
1. Event General Information:
The Task Owner shall fill the Event General Information section, and specify the
following information:
Event Title
• Charging Code
Event Date
• WBS
Event Country/ Location/ City
• Task
Event Type
• Team Leader
Face-Face or virtual event
• Task Owner
Project Name
• Finance Officer
• Country Focal Point (To be notified)
Department
• Venue type
2. Event Programmatic Information
The Task Owner shall fill the Programmatic Information Section, and specify the
following information:
Event Objectives
• Material sharing methodology
Event Description
• Agenda
Methods
• Facilitators Meeting Details
Topics Covered

Preliminary Participants (adding invitees
list)
Time
Resource(s) (e.g., Trainer, Facilitator,
Lecturer, Consultant, etc.)
Food & Beverage
Participating Partners / Organizations
with Contact (Email, Phone)
Number of People Attending
Event Needs Training Materials Check?
Any Additional Requirements
Materials Link
Location
3. Event Logistics & Administration Information
The Task Owner shall fill the Logistics & Administration Section in coordination with
the Operation Officer and other involved teams indicating the below information for the
event. In case an Operations Officer was delegated to fill this part, proper coordination
between the Operations Officer and the Task Owner shall take place.
Expected # of Participants
• Media and Communication
Requirements
Expected # of GHD|EMPHNET Staff
• Translation requirements (Interpretation
Translation or Documents Translation)
Expected # of Facilitators
• Transportation requirements and details
Expected # of Administrator
• Passengers Information
Event Size
• Airplane for Participants’ details
Seating Style
• Airplane for Staff details
Equipment and Materials
• Hotel for Participants’ details
IT Equipment and Materials
• Hotel for GHD|EMPHNET Staff details
Needed IT Support Staff
• Food and Beverage details
Needed Zoom Meeting Request
• Pre-event website announcement
News article on website
• Newsletter article
Social media coverage
• Press and TV coverage
Rollup/banner/pop-up
• Photographer/ Videographer
The above-filled information shall get the approval of the Technical Team Leader,
Technical Director, and Project Management Office to ensure their compliance with
the event plan. In addition, Finance Affairs plays a crucial role in checking the event
allocated budget covers and approve, to proceed with event conduct.
All GHD|EMPNET events shall be approved by the Executive Director before their
conduction.
General Polices:
Amendments:

o If there was an amendment that is related to internal support and not
related to the event budget, such as requesting for a Website Article,
then the Task Owner shall share this update through email with the
concerned department keeping the respected Team Leader/ Director in
the cc.
o If there was an amendment that is related to all concerned parties such
as event dates, no. of participants or events no. of days, then the Task
Owner shall share this update through email with all concerned
departments keeping the respected Team Leader/ Director in the cc. If
there was any change to the budget, then the Finance Officer/ Manager
shall revise budget and provide their approvals before proceeding with
the event.
As a general role, when there is a cascade of trainings in one activity, it is
preferable to initiated as one event, if the Task Owner sees that it is better to
make it as a sperate events (for example, there is long time span between the
trainings which may affect the logistics preparation), prior discussion and
agreement with the Team Leader/ Direct shall take place.
Not all the items mentioned below are mandatory to be applied to all events,
this depends on the Task Owner decision based on the event nature,
requirements and complexity. This shall be clearly stated when the Task Owner
fills the Event Request items (Annex 01).
Event Material Guideline (Annex 02) provide a general guideline for the Task
Owner regarding the requirements for Media and Communications functions.
For simple meetings where there is no travel or accommodation, Task Owner
may fill Meeting Request instead of Event Request. The meeting request is
designed to request only the needed information to conduct a simple meeting,
However, it still requires the same level of approvals as the event.

nodes.heading: Event Announcement
nodes.own_text:
In some instances, such as regional workshops or conferences, it is necessary to
announce for an event on the website and different channels for the public audience
where registration is required. In these instances, the Task Owner shall determine the
need for event announcement based on the event audience. The announcement shall
be prepared by the Task Owner at least six weeks prior to the scheduled event and
shall be reviewed by the Team Leader, Director, and then the Executive Director. The
announcement should have the following information consistent/in line with the initial
concept note, activity description, and other relevant technical documents:
Title of event
Dates and location of event
Objective of the event and its context
Any required pre-requisites for participants
Closing date for application
Any expected fees incurred in attending the event

Registration Application form, if any.
Once the announcement is approved, it shall be published by the Media and
Communication Team at GHD|EMPHNET’s announcement channels.

nodes.heading: Event Language
nodes.own_text:
GHD|EMPHNTE events could be conducted in English, Arabic or French based on the
audience. However, if the need arises for interpretation from one language into
another for the audience, then the Task Owner shall request this added service upon
filling the event request.

nodes.heading: Participants
nodes.own_text:
Participant Identification process shall start four weeks before the event through
participants nomination/ invitation or registration:
1. Participants Nomination
In the case where the target audience names/ titles are not specified, it is
necessary to prepare a letter to target countries/ organizations to ask for
nominations as soon as the event is scheduled. The Task Owner shall specify such
need and share the nomination list with the Operations Officer.
The letter shall list the event details and to request to share the names, titles and
contact information for the nominated candidates.
2. Participants Invitation
When participants titles or names are identified, then invitation letters shall be
shared with their entities or directly to the participants sharing the related event
details and request participants to confirm their attendance.
Both nomination letters and invitation letters shall be prepared by the Task Owner,
reviewed by the Team Leader/ Director and signed by the Executive Director. Once
the letter is approved from the technical team, the Operations Officer shall provide the
required coordination with the Administrative Team till the issuance of the letter
applying the approved policies and procedures for official letters issuance as per
Administrative Affairs Policies & Procedures Manual (ML-ADM-01).
Letters shall be shared through the Administrative email keeping the Task Owner,
Team Leader/ Director, Country Focal Point and Operations Officer in the cc to follow
up receiving the response. In this email, the Country Focal Point or the Task Owner
shall be mentioned as a reference in case of any enquiries.
In certain cases, the letters shall be sent as official mail, policies in Administrative
Affairs Policies & Procedures Manual (ML-ADM-01) shall be followed.
The response for the letters may take time depending on the logistics criteria and
process in the different countries, however, sometimes it is necessary to send

reminders based on the Task Owner decision. The Operations Officer shall update the
Participants list according to the invitee’s response and keep the Task Owner
informed. The participants list shall include all the required information that required
for the Technical Team and Finance and Accounting Team such as the origin of the
participant, the requirement for per diem (including the number of days with departure
and arrival dates) and ground transportation, and to specify if there is any exceptional
need. These pieces of information are important to ensure accurate Financial
calculations; any changes will lead to change request.
The Operations Officer shall keep tracking on the responses and update the
Participants Lists accordingly.
Letters issuance shall follow the applied policies and procedures for official letters
issuance at GHD|EMPHNET as per Administrative Affairs Policies & Procedures
Manual (ML-ADM-01). Note: In certain cases, based on the recipient, the letter could
be shared from Task Owner Email.
3. Registration
In rare cases, registration could be open for public through announcing the event at
GHD|EMPHNET different channels. Registration application or system shall be
developed by the Innovative Solutions Team under the recommendations of the Task
Owner.
Whenever the event is announced for public registration, received applications will be
studied to select the eligible participants. In this case, confirmation letter/ email for
registration shall be shared with the participants. Support letters shall be shared based
on the need.
Participants Bio Data
In order to have an updated database of participants who were involved in
GHD|EMPHNET events, it is essential to have the biodata of the participants (Names,
Gender, Date of Birth, Email Address, Mobile number, educational degree, Major,
Total Experience, Country of Work, Current Job Title, Current Employer, Experience
in current position, languages, etc.). Whenever these data are not available, a Biodata
form to collect the required data shall be prepared by the Operations Officer based on
the Task Owner recommendations.
The link is shared with participants along with the welcoming email providing a
deadline.
NOTE: It is extremely important to maintain accurate records of participants in the
EMPHNET Resources Engine (ERE), which is a site intending to collect data for all
participants who were involved in any of GHD|EMPHNET activities (including the past
events). After each event, any new participants shall be added to the ERE. However,

extreme caution must be taken not to add duplicates to the records as this will strain
the ERE system resources and will require a lot of efforts later on for duplication
removals and updating of new data for the records of the same individuals (as opposed
to adding the same individuals multiple times).

nodes.heading: Facilitators and Speakers
nodes.own_text:
The Task Owner is responsible for communication with speakers or facilitators. This
should be done at an early stage. Once secured, facilitators or speakers are given a
deadline for sending their presentations. Travel arrangements for facilitators or
speakers follow the same procedure as that of the participants.

nodes.heading: Venue Selection
nodes.own_text:
Events venue could be at the premises of the trainees such as Ministries, or at
GHD|EMPHNET premises or there would be a need to rent a venue. This
should be specified in the planning phase.
If the training is at the premises of the target entities in the countries, The
Government counterpart institution e.g. MOH will do the necessary
arrangements in coordination with GHD|EMPHNET representative at the
country.
If there is a need to rent a venue, the Operations Officer or our representative
in the country should request three quotations for venue rental at least four
weeks prior to the dates of the event taking the following into consideration:
o Number of days needed to conduct the event.
o Estimated number of participants (including facilitators and any other
support staff)
o Estimated number of rooms for accommodating participants and facilitators,
if any.
o Number of meeting rooms and their setting/s (including breakout rooms), if
any.
o Need for special arrangements, such as head table, podium, flip charts, etc.
o Needed equipment, such as computer, projector, sound system,
microphones, wireless connection, IT technical support, etc. If not provided
by the venue, a sound system organization shall be outsourced.
o Food and beverages required for the event.
Note: The cost of renting meeting rooms is often waived by hotels when
catering (lunch and coffee breaks) is offered for charge. Therefore, make
sure to include the catering services needed during the meeting/s.
o Other relevant information required for event conduct.
Once the quotations are received, they shall be analyzed by the Operations
Officer considering the following points:
o Availability of spacious meeting rooms (enough space to move around
conveniently)

o Good lighting, acoustics, ventilation, heating/air-conditioning, breakout area
and parking.
o Meeting venue/room is close and/or easily accessible to the hotel rooms.
o Meeting venue is close or easily accessible to the office during potentially
heavy traffic hours.
o Availability of support service, such as IT, photocopying, wireless
connection.
o Hotel policy blocking rooms, reservation, and cancelation.
o Dates for confirming reservations and any financial liability in this regard.
o Country’s counterpart recommendation.
Note: Many hotels offer a free suite or room with group booking (over a
particular number). This is a complimentary service that GHD|EMPHNET
can seize if needed.
The following shall be taken into consideration while selecting a venue:
o The Operations Officer or our representative in the country shall make
sure that the venue is not booked the day before the event, in order to
make the required setup the day before the event. This is crucial in the
case that audio-visual (AV) equipment/system (Sound system,
Videography and/or Photography) should be implemented as it needs
time and can’t be implemented in the same day of the event. Otherwise,
the Operations Officer shall make the required arrangements with the
venue to make sure that the venue is ready before the event.
o For events where accommodation of participants is necessary, it is
recommended that the selected venue be in the same premises as hotel
rooms. Transportation should be arranged if venue location is other than
that of accommodation. Note: Every effort should be made to avoid such
situation in order to minimize logistics efforts.
The proposed offers and the above analysis shall be shared with the Creative
Unit to provide their specialized opinion regarding halls suitability for event
conduct. Based on the setup of the event, number of participants and lighting
of the halls, the Creative Lead will recommend the options that are suitable for
the event. The Task Owner shall select one of the proposed options.
The proposed option(s) shall be shared by the Operations Officer with Finance
Specialist/ Officer for recommended decision based on the available budget.
Based on the aforementioned feedback, the Task Owner shall take the decision
regarding the venue selection.
Once the venue is selected and the rates are agreed upon, a contract is signed
with the hotel after confirming that all needs are covered in the contract. The
Operations Officer or our representative in the country will send the signed
contract to the hotel indicating that the point of contact with the hotel from this
point on will be the Operations Officer or our representative in the country. This
is preferably done by an email, keeping the Finance in the cc.

Getting three quotations for venue could be waived in the case that
GHD|EMPHNET have a general agreement with venues or there was a clear
justification for sole sourcing and/or selecting a certain venue.

nodes.heading: Travel Arrangements
nodes.note: contains sub-blocks Passports, Visa Issuances, Travel Booking, Accommodation, Ground Transportation - not split further, kept as one leaf since not TOC-listed separately
nodes.own_text:
For events where travel and accommodation of participants, facilitators or
GHD|EMPHNET staff is necessary (such as regional events), arrangements should
be made as soon as nominated candidates are identified. The Operations Officer is
responsible for travel arrangements, however, s/he shall share the travel information
and updates on regular basis and notify the Task Owner of any potential problems
Passports
For external flights, valid passports shall be available for the concerned
person(s).
The Operations team shall check GHD|EMPHNET data base for the availability
of valid passports copies before contacting the concerned persons. Valid
passport should have validity of at least six months of the travel date.
If a passport copy is available in our database; share an email with the
concerned person(s) to confirm that the available copy is the latest valid
passport, and he/she confirms to use it.
If no passport copy is available in our database, then the Operations Officer
shall contact the concerned person(s) requesting them to share it.
Passports copies shall be kept in DMS Twenty, under the administration
channel, in the Passports folder under the relevant country.
Passport copies shall be saved with the first and last name of the concerned
person.
If passport copies in the database are outdated, they must be updated/replaced
by new copies within the same record.
Visa Issuances
The need for visa issuance for participants, facilitator or GHD|EMPHNET staff
shall be identified at early stage because in some cases it might take longer
than three weeks to obtain a visa. This shall be done by the Operations Officer
usually in coordination with the Task Owner.
To ensure that the Operations Officer has the correct and valid information in
order to proceed with visa issuance and travel booking, a form (Annex 03) shall
be shared with participants and facilitators requesting them to fill the required
information. Form content could be updated based on the requirements.
The following scenarios for visa issuance could take place:
Some countries request visitors to present a letter from GHD|EMPHNET to
verify their attendance at an event. In such cases, GHD|EMPHNET Operations
Officer issues visa support letters to participants (or facilitators) attending the

event, at least 2 weeks prior to the event. The information below should be
included in these letters:
o Full name (as it appears on participant’s passport)
o GHD|EMPHNET’s full name, title, and dates of the event that the
participant intends to attend.
o Include a fax number or email address for any information request
For events conducted in Jordan and for those participants and facilitators who
come from countries where there is no Jordan embassy, GHD|EMPHNET
needs to support these by facilitating issuing their visas from Jordan’s
government.
The Operations Officer prepares the visa letters, signed by the Executive
Director and submit it to Ministry of Interior (MoI). Follow up with the MoI should
be through the focal point in coordination with the Operations Officer.
For events conducted outside Jordan, the Operations Officer shall make the
required arrangements for visa issuance. However, in certain cases, visa
issuance could be supported by our representative in the country, while the
Operations Officer holds the responsibility of follow up and tracking.
Travel Booking
The required information shall be compiled by the Operations Officer and
shared with travel agency to procced with reservations. In certain cases, the
Operations Officer can arrange for travel booking in coordination with the
Country Representative or travel agency based on the country requirements.
It is important to take note of the following when making flight reservations:
o Check that the passport expiry date is at least six months from the event
date, plus any other visa requirements (for certain countries) are met.
No ticket shall be issued without obtaining a copy of the passport.
o The visa is issued and valid, if required.
o The route of travel is convenient and accurate.
o Travel insurance is issued, if required by the country requirements.
o Any additional entry requirements.
In some cases, the participants or facilitators may request amending the ticket
for personal reasons, the Operations Officer shall connect the travel agency
with the participant to proceed with the change(s) and fees payment. However,
GHD|EMPHNET is not responsible for extending participants/ facilitators stay
period.
Accommodation
The Operations Officer shall make sure to reserve hotel rooms for participants,
facilitators, and GHD|EMPHNET staff who confirm attending the event.
Accommodation information shall be shared with the participants along with
travel details.

In certain cases, where the event is conducted in countries other than Jordan,
the Operations Officer can arrange for hotel booking in coordination with the
Country Representative or travel agency.
In some cases, the participant may request to amend the hotel reservation
dates or type of room for personal reasons, in this case the Operations Officer
shall make the required arrangements with the hotel and the participant shall
pay the extra fees to the hotel directly.
Ground Transportation
The Operations Officer shall make the required arrangements for participants
regarding transportation inside Jordan.
Outside Jordan, ground transportation fees will be given to participants.

nodes.heading: Welcoming Participants
nodes.own_text:
Once all the arrangements are completed, the Operations Officer will send a
welcoming email to the participants including visa (if required), ticket, accommodation
details, travel guide, agenda, biodata link, the location of the event and any additional
information at least one week before the event start. The Task Owner, Project
Manager, and Country Presentative shall be kept in the cc.
Note: The language of the email (Arabic, English) shall be based on the audience. The
Task Owner may share the email from his/ her end based on the target audience.

nodes.heading: Event Materials
nodes.note: contains Agenda, Training Material, Name tags/Table tags sub-blocks - kept as one leaf
nodes.own_text:
Materials such as agenda, training material, presentations, and references shall be
prepared in advance for the event. If needed as physical copies, the final versions
need to be made available for printing and photocopying at least one week prior to the
event undertaking; the Task Owner is responsible for preparing a folder prototype of
these material and to give it to the Operations Officer to make appropriate copies and
preparations. In addition, event presentation(s) shall be provided three days before
the event. Creative Lead could be consulted regarding material branding.
The Task Owner shall give the presentations to the Information Technology Team or
the representative in the country in a folder named by day number, e.g. Day I, Day 2,
Day 3. When saving the presentation add to the name of the presentation file a number
at the beginning of the file name that matches the order of that presentation. For
Example: save a presentation to be presented second in row on the third day of the
event (as per the agenda) carrying the file name “Outbreak Response” should be
saved in a folder named “Day 3” with the name “2. Outbreak Response”
The Task Owner shall specify the method for sharing the event material with
participants whether to be printed, through a link, or through a USB. It is preferable to
go green and to share the material through links.

If there is a need to add any entity(ies) logo(s) to the approved template or there is a
need, the Task Owner shall get the approval of the Team Leader then to share the
request with the Creative Lead who in his/ her turn will refer to the internal brand
guideline and the level of contribution of the other entity.
The Task Owner is responsible for preparing the event’s agenda in accordance
with the intended objectives using the approved template. It is recommended
to build in an approximate 30 minutes of daily “hidden” time in order to
accommodate late start or any running over of time for any of the sessions. It
is often necessary to secure facilitators’ agreement to their scheduled
presentations (sessions) prior to finalizing the agenda.
Once the agenda is approved by the Team Leader (Executive Director approval
shall be obtained based on the Team Leader or the Director decision) it is
shared with the relevant stakeholders and facilitators or speakers. In addition,
it should be shared with the Operations Officer in order to facilitate preparation
of venue premises.
Agenda could be prepared and distributed digitally. Annex 02 provides general
guidelines regarding event material management.
Note: For large events (please refer to Annex 02), the final agenda shall be
shared with the Creative Lead for final design and printing.
Training Material
Training material shall be prepared in advance using the approved template.
All training material shall be checked by the Capacity Building team before they
are used at any event. Task Owner shall share the link of the training materials
at least four weeks before the event to give some time for materials check. The
material shall be updated according to the received comments from the
Capacity Building team and the Final Material shall be shared with the
Operations Officer accordingly.
Pretest, posttest, evaluation material, and online surveys shall be prepared by
the Task Owner and shared with the Operations Officer at least two weeks in
advance. The Operations Officer will launch the aforementioned material on the
approved tool and provide the Task Owner with the appropriate link to be used
for the event.
Name tags/ Table tags
The final list of participants shall be shared by the Operations Officer at least 5
days before the event with the Media and Communication team to prepare the
name tags (Badge) for the participants and the facilitators and the table tags for
the facilitators, any updates shall be shared by the Operations Officer on timely
basis.

The Media and Communication Team are responsible to make the design for
the name tags and table tags, while the Operations Officer or the representative
in the county should print them and make them ready to be delivered to
participants and facilitators.
For events outside Jordan, these items could be printed in Jordan and shipped
depending in the logistics in that country.

nodes.path: Section 01 > 1.4 Policies > Media and Communication Role
nodes.heading: Media and Communication Role
nodes.note: contains Publicity, Photography, Rollups, AV, Plaque, Promotional Material sub-blocks
nodes.own_text:
Annex 02 summarizes the difference between the event sizes; the size of the event
will determine the required branded material to be prepared for the event. The
following items shall be specified in the event request based on the event needs:
Publicity and Media Coverage
Based on the event, the Task Owner shall request the required publicity and
media coverage for an event.
Task Owner should provide timely media content material to the Media and
Communication team.
Policies and Procedures in Media and Communication Manual (ML-MAC-01)
shall be applied.
Photography and Videography Selection
The Operations Officer in coordination with Task Owner shall specify the
needed coverage for the event:
o Photos, videos, or both could be required for the event.
o If the photographer shall cover the whole event either for Photography
or Videography (to ensure video recording availability), then an
outsourcing photographer will be contacted. On the other hand, if the
materials are for promotional purposes only, an internal or external
photographer will be assigned.
It is the responsibility of the Creative Lead to supervise the supplier process
based on the desired material from each event. The creative lead will also guide
the supplier on the needed material/converge.
If the event is outside Jordan:
o The Operations Officer/ Task Owner shall do the required arrangements
with country representative to arrange for photography/ videography in
collaboration with the Creative Lead.
o In certain cases where the event is outside Jordan, the Task Owner or
the representative in the country will take the photos follow, however,
they shall adhere to GHD|EMPHNET photography guidelines (GL-MC-
03)
o The taken photos should highlight the major activities of the event.
Photos/videos should capture presentations, attendees, speakers,
group work, registration, handing certificates and other activities. If the
Task Owner/ Operations Officer took the photos, then they shall share
them with the MaC team via email. The MaC team is responsible for filing

the photos on the shared drive in the appropriate folder on the
Documentation Management System (DMS Twenty).
o The Operations Officer coordinator sharing the events photos and
videos with the participants upon request.
Rollups/ Banners/ Backdrops/ Pop-ups
Annex 02 summarizes the criteria for rollups/ banners/ backdrops/ pop-up setup
during the event. This shall provide the required guide for the involved teams
to assure standardization among events and this will assure the required
visibility.
If the event is outside Jordan, then the Country Office representative or the
focal point at the country shall print the designed items by the HQ Media and
Communication Team and place them according to the guideline.
Audio-visual (AV) System and Interpretation
If a sound system and/or real-time interpretation are required for an event, it is
the responsibility of the Media and Communication team to select the vendor.
Three quotations shall be requested from vendors for any event. The Media
and Communication team is responsible to select the suitable vendor in
coordination with the Finance Team.
Providing three quotations could be waived in the case there was signed
contracts with sound system vendors.
Once the vendor is selected, then all relevant parties shall be notified, and the
Operations Officer shall make the required arrangements with the vendor.
Plaque
GHD|EMPHNET branded plaques are only to be handed out during mediocre
and large events (during the opening or closing ceremonies) in one of the
following conditions:
o Closing an event for a long-term project
o EMPHNET’s biennial conferences
o C-level executive representation of the partner
Plaques can be handed to:
o Organizations such as Ministries (ministers), international organizations
and the private sector.
o People for their distinguished contribution.
o Service providers: such as travel agencies, event planners, etc.
It is important to bear in mind that plaques are not handed in the following
situations:
o During training and workshops
o During private meeting
o New partnerships (only during closing ceremonies when the projects are
completed)
o When GHD|EMPHNET is not the host
o When there is any political sensitivity

o Plaques are never handed out to donors.
GHD|EMPHNET plaques are in two sizes, the regular size is handed out to
partners while the large size is handed out to C-Level
The names and the content of the plaque shall be provided by the task owner
after obtaining approval by the Executive Director.
The branding of the plaques shall follow GHD|EMPHNET branding guidelines
For large events the Media and Communication team may assign an event agency
for the event setup, however, the sound system could be outsourced separately.
For Large events, the Creative Lead shall make sure that all the planned setups
are in place before the event till the event end to assure proper visibility.
Promotional Material
In the case there was a need for promotional material for an event, then the policy for
promotional materials in Media and Communication Manual (ML-MAC-01) shall be
followed.

nodes.heading: Certificates
nodes.own_text:
Certificates Preparation
Media and Communication team shall be notified about the event once the
event is approved over the system, however, two weeks before the certificates
delivery, the Operations Officer should share with the Media and
Communication team the event official name, event date, the official event
language, certificates serial number, the other entity(ies) logo and name and
position of signatory. In addition, the list of attendees shall be shared once
finalized maximum 5 days before the event.
Serial numbers for certificates:
o Serial numbers for digital certificates are assigned by the Operations
Officer (using the approved sheet between the Creative Lead and
Operations Officers).
o Serial numbers for printed certificates are already printed on the
templates, Operations Officer shall track the serial numbers for
documentation purpose.
o Serial number for FETP certificates should be provided by the
Operations Officer as follows:
Country acronyms-FETP modality-Cohort number-Serial Number
For example:
EGY-FETP-01-1
EGY-IFETP-01-1
EGY-BFETP-01-1
Media and Communication team shall prepare the certificate design according
to GHD|EMPHNET guidelines, and share it with the Task Owner, whom by

his/her turn will share it with the other entities, if any, to get their approval and
to agree on the signature method (live signature, e-signature through
GHD|EMPHNET, e-signature through the entity itself).
MaC team will start inserting the names to the certificate’s template and
inserting the certificate serial number as shared by the Operations Officer.
The Operations Officer shall review all the names and serial number on the
certificates prior signing and printing.
Note: If there is a change to the approved templates as requested by other
entities, then Creative Lead will take approval from the Executive Director.
Certificates Signing
Based on the selected signatory method of the other entity(ies):
o If all parties are going to sign the certificated electronically, then the final
certificates will be signed by the other entity(ies) first, after being
approved by the Team Leader, The Task Owner shall communicate with
the Creative Lead for adding the Executive Director signature.
o If the other entity(ies) will sign live, then the Creative Lead will add the
Executive Director's signature upon confirmation from the Task Owner,
then certificates will be printed to be shared by the other entity.
Certificates could be prepared and distributed digitally to each participant,
based on the Task Owner decision.
The approval of the Executive Director for the event implies authorization of the
Creative Lead to use the Executive Director e-signature for certificates issuance
after obtaining the Task Owner and Team Leader approval on the certificates.
Certificates Printing
FETP certificates are printed in the country of the program implementation.
GHD|EMPHNET and EMPHNET certificates other than FETP certificates shall
be printed in the Headquarters only. They can be shipped through courier or
sent with any team member.
GHD|EMPHNET and EMPHNET certificates hard copy templates are the
responsibility of the Creative Lead to prepare, add serial numbers, stamp, and
print.
The Custody and Inventory team is responsible for notifying the Creative Lead
when the hard copy certificates inventory is lower than 50 certificates.

nodes.heading: Certificate Documentation
nodes.own_text:
The Operations Officer shall maintain certificates documentation for all
certificates (printed, digital or FETP certificates).

The Operations Officer shall make the required arrangements for any side meetings,
facilitator meetings or Gala dinner that is related to the Event, based on the Task
Owner or the Executive Director request.
Annex 04 summarizes a checklist that shall be followed up by the Operations Officer
to support them to assure that the preparation phase is going on timely manner and
as planned.

nodes.heading: 2.1. Purpose
nodes.own_text: activities that shall take place before launching the event and during the event.

nodes.heading: 2.2. Scope
nodes.own_text:
Conducting a successful event, required team effort, multitask management, and
effective communication. It is also required good skills for problem solving to face any
challenges during the event. The following topics are standard issues that need to be
considered when conducting an event to take place in regular and steady
circumstances. This policy applies to all personnel involved in running the event.

nodes.heading: 2.3. Responsibilities
nodes.own_text:
It is the responsibility of the Operations Officer or the representative in the
country (who is responsible to logistical support) to be available during the
entire event to assure proper implementation of the planned items.
It is the responsibility of the Logistics Officer to provide the required support to
the Operations Officer prior, during, and after the event (This is mainly inside
Jordan).
It is the responsibility of the Task Owner to ensure the event according to the
agenda and the plan. Based on the event, the Task Owner shall attend the
event or coordinate with the Technical representative in the country to attend.

nodes.path: Section 02 > 2.4 Policies > Before Launching the event
nodes.heading: Before Launching the event
nodes.own_text:
To assure smooth implementation, every effort shall be made before the event
to make sure that all the required arrangements are made to achieve the
requirements that was requested in the planning phase. Each team member
plays a crucial role in making the success of the event as follows.
Event Site check shall be performed by the assigned team one day before the
event to make sure that the set up matches the requirements and to give time
to rectify any incident(s).
In addition, the relevant team shall be one hour and half before the event start
time on the first day to reassure proper arrangements.
The involved team in these preparations are usually the Operations Officer,
Logistics Officer, IT Specialist, plus a technical officer. However, based on the
circumstances and event location and country these functions could be
delegated to the representative in the country or other personnel. However, this
shall be monitored by the Operations Officer.

nodes.heading: During the Event
nodes.next_heading: Delivering Payments to Participants and Facilitators
nodes.own_text:
t
The Operations Officer or the representative in the country and the Logistics
Officer should be always physically present during the event. They shall arrive
one hour before starting the daily program (other than the first day) to make the
required arrangements and should be the last one to leave the premises.
The Operations Officer could request support from the Logistics Officer in
accomplishing any task or arrangements, however, the Operations Officer
holds the ultimate responsibility.
The Task Owner and/ or the Technical Team at the country should arrive to the
event site at least one hour prior to the start time to make sure that all the
required arrangements are in place.
Media and Communication team member(s) should attend the opening session
of the event and take appropriate notes and/ or photos.
The Creative Lead shall make sure that the venue setup and all arrangements
are as planned.

nodes.path: Section 02 > 2.4 Policies > Delivering Payments to Participants and Facilitators
nodes.heading: Delivering Payments to Participants and Facilitators
nodes.own_text:
The Operations Officer shall coordinate delivering the payment with the
accounting department.
In the case that participants and facilitators attending events are entitled to a
per diem covering their period of stay. The Treasury Accountant or a delegate
is responsible for preparing and delivering these per diems.
Delivering the per diem shall be on the second day of the event for the events
that for more than one day. The Treasury Accountant or a delegate shall make
sure to distribute the per diem in a suitable time that doesn’t disturb the event
itself or the participants/ facilitators.
When the event is conducted outside Jordan, the Treasury Accountant shall
make the required coordination with the assigned person who will deliver the
payment to participants.
Accounting policies and procedures shall be applied.

nodes.heading: Social Program
nodes.own_text:
It is not customary for GHD|EMPHNET to offer social activities or a social
program during the event. However, GHD|EMPHNET’s Operations Officer or
the country representative is responsible for arranging trips or providing
information to any of the participants who wish to do sightseeing. Sometimes,
the participants wish to engage in a group dinner that is self-paid. In such
instances, the Operations Officer is responsible for making dinner reservations
for the group. Other times, GHD|EMPHNET Executive Office decides to invite
some of the participants or facilitators to a farewell and recognition dinner, for
which the Operations Officer will arrange reservations and inform the
concerned parties of details.

nodes.heading: Photography
nodes.own_text:
y
Based on the arrangements during the preparation phase, the Media and
Communication team is responsible for ensuring that photos are captured to cover the
event whether this is done internally or by an external photographer, by the
representative in the country or by the Task owner/ Operations Officer who attend the
event.

nodes.heading: 2.7. Related Documents
nodes.own_text: s

nodes.heading: 3.1. Purpose
nodes.own_text: activities that shall take place upon event closure.

nodes.heading: 3.2. Scope
nodes.own_text:
All events come to a conclusion and certain actions are required to wrap an event in
order to assure documentation of outcomes and achievements. Concluding an event
is not a sudden and rapid action as several issues need to be considered. This section
summarizes the issues need to be considered to assure proper and efficient closing
of events. This policy applies to all personnel involved in event conduct closeout.

nodes.heading: 3.3. Responsibilities
nodes.own_text:
It is the responsibility of the Task Owner and the Operations Officer to assure proper
close out of the event.

nodes.heading: Certificates and Plaque
nodes.own_text:
Whenever certificates are requested for an event, participants and facilitators are
handed Certificates denoting their attendance. The Executive Director or someone
nominated by the Executive Director shall deliver the certificates.
In certain cases, certificates can be distributed digitally to the participants.
In certain occasions and based on the Technical Team Leader decision, Plaque could
be handed out at the end of the event.

nodes.heading: Event Items
nodes.own_text:
Event items that are on the event site shall be collected after the event. This is under
the responsibility of the Operations Officer or the representative in the country. The
Logistics Officer shall provide the required support in coordination with the Operations
Officer.

nodes.heading: Payments
nodes.own_text:
The Operations Officer needs to present receipts retained from conducting the event
to the Finance Department together. The Treasury Accountant is responsible for
finalizing payment to the hotel or event site. S/he is responsible for cross-checking the
final guest list received from the hotel with the list provided by the Operations Officer.
The Treasury Accountant and any employee who received invoices shall submit them
to the Accounting team which by their turn will check them and upload them to the
system. After that the Finance Team shall record them to the relevant activity and
issue any required reports.

nodes.heading: Reporting
nodes.own_text:
g
Upon completing the event, the Task Owner is responsible for conducting a close-out
meeting with all relevant staff who were engaged in managing the event. The purpose
of this meeting is to discuss the event to identify and discuss any gaps or limitations
faced during the workshop. These meetings will help in identifying lessons learnt.
The Task Owner is responsible for preparing a report summarizing the event
proceedings (Technical report). This report should be prepared using GHD|EMPHNET
report template and should be presented for the Team Leader/ Director within two
weeks from concluding the event through the system. Once reviewed and approved,
the report should be saved in its relevant folder on the DMS Twenty. The Task Owner
is also responsible for saving the material used during the event.
Documents Keeping
The Operations Officer is responsible for event documentation on the following sites:
DMS Twenty/ Administration/ Project Tracking, by creating a new item
detailing the event details. This tracking is used for report generation and
projects tracking.
Project Center/ Project Activity, by creating a new folder and name it
according to the event name, adding the final documents related to the event
such as actual participants list, agenda, training material, and technical report.
EMPHNET Resources Engine (ERE), this site aims to collect data for all
participants who were involved in any of GHD|EMPHNET activities (including
the past events). After each event, any new participants shall be added to the
ERE.
Additional Consideration: It is extremely important to maintain accurate records
of participants in the EMPHNET Resources Engine (ERE) when collecting data
for participants of any event as they may also be involved in similar past
events/activities. After each event, any new participants shall be added to the
ERE. However, extreme caution must be practiced not to add duplicates to the
records as this will strain the ERE system resources and will require a lot of
efforts later on for duplication removals and updating of new data for the records
of the same individuals (as opposed to adding the same individuals multiple
times).
In addition, the Project Management Team shall update the Project Center with the
event actual information.
Media and Communications team shall upload all the designs and photos related to
the event on the DMS Twenty.
The Technical team are responsible for saving the event training material on the DMS
Twenty.

The Information Technology, upon request from the Task Owner, shall keep the
recording of virtual events conducted through Zoom in MS Stream for future reference.
